newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bid $67,passed-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bid $67,passed-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $67.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00, feedlot sources said.

Packers raised bids $1.00 following light sales late Wednesday at $67.00, they said. About 4,500 head sold after 1500 CST in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, several feedlot managers said.

The managers said owners remained confident that packers would pay $68.00 sometime Thursday. Fed cattle prices were expected to be underpinned by ideas packers needed to book cattle for operations after the Easter holiday weekend.
Outlooks for firm fed cattle prices also were generated by active beef movement on Wednesday, although packers had to discount prices to move the product, feedlot sources said.
Beef prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.57 to $0.96 per cwt, with 369 fabricated beef loads sold.
Smaller numbers of cattle on showlists, compared with last week, also could underpin fed cattle prices, they said.
However, projections for higher cattle prices could be offset by ideas that packers next week will be able to take delivery of cash cattle contracted for April, the sources said.
